messages:
bob_customer: Hey @support, our staging service started returning 401 invalid_api_key right after we rotated the env var during today's deploy. No code changes. Need help asap — traffic failing in the deploy window.

bob_customer: Repro from one of our pods:
```
curl -v -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -H \"Api-Key: sk_test_7kLmN8QvX2uYz\\\"\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}

bob_customer: We think the key was put into Vault via a CI script. It looks like there's a trailing backslash in the stored value (maybe escaped during a Windows -> shell copy). The key should be 32 chars but seems off.

alice_support: Thanks for reporting — can you paste the last 6 characters of the key (masked) and one recent request-id from the failing request? Also, which header are you using in your app (Authorization vs Api-Key)?

bob_customer: Header is `Api-Key`. Last 6 chars on the env var we set: `...X2uYz\` (there's a trailing backslash showing up in our config UI). Request id from the failing request (from our logs): `req_01G7m5Q8A9`.

support-bot: Incident log: 1716200003 - request req_01G7m5Q8A9 returned 401 invalid_api_key for customer org id org_42.

charlie_eng: That trailing backslash will change the token bytes — it becomes part of the string. In many shells `"` sequence can get inserted or a Windows CR/LF or escape can leave a `\` char. Two quick checks:
- On the running pod, run: `echo -n "$API_KEY" | hexdump -C` to inspect bytes.
- Or check secret raw value in Vault/Secret Manager via UI (don't paste full key here) and confirm no trailing `\\`.

dan_sre: Also check your CI template: if you interpolate with JSON and don't strip quotes you can end up with a backslash escape. Example bug we saw: `echo \"$KEY\" > secret` when used in a Windows step produced a literal `\\` sequence.

alice_support: If you can share a minimal repro (curl) from a host that isn't behind your sidecar, that helps rule out proxy modification. Try `curl -H "Api-Key: $(cat /run/secrets/redwood_api_key)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` and paste the exact curl output (masking key). Also include HTTP response headers we return (we can look for our `x-redwood-request-id`).

bob_customer: Ran the hexdump on the pod:
```
00000000  73 6b 5f 74 65 73 74 5f  37 6b 4c 6d 4e 38 51 76  |sk_test_7kLmN8QvX2u|
00000010  59 7a 5c                                       |Yz\\|
```
So it's definitely a trailing 0x5c (backslash). We patched the secret in Vault (removed the backslash) and restarted the deployment; still checking.

support-bot: 1716201100 - observed repeated 401s for req_01G7m5Q8A9; error invalid_api_key.

charlie_eng: When you fix the secret, you can validate without redeploy by exec-ing into a pod and doing `curl -H "Api-Key: $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health`.

bob_customer: Confirmed — after removing the trailing backslash in Vault and restarting pods, same curl returns 200 and body `{\"status\":\"ok\"}`. Deploy looks healthy now. :white_check_mark:

alice_support: Glad that fixed it. Root cause: malformed secret with trailing backslash introduced during CI/migration. Recommendation: add a validation step in your rotation pipeline to check token length and reject values with control characters. Also avoid embedding keys in JSON strings without proper escaping.

dan_sre: I'll follow up with a small CI lint PR template we use that checks for non-alphanumeric chars in API tokens and warns. If you want, we can also rotate this key to invalidate the bad copy and ensure there are no cached instances.

bob_customer: Appreciate the quick help — please close the ticket from your side when convenient. Thanks everyone! :tada:
